desc: CAST IN HEATERS Cast-in heaters are precision-engineered heaters formed by casting resistance elements (typically nickel-chrome) into aluminum, bronze, or other alloys. They provide uniform heat transfer and are ideal for applications requiring complex shapes or high thermal conductivity. Operating at temperatures up to 1200°F (649°C), they are often used in plastic and metal processing. View Brochure

MICA BAND HEATERS Mica band heaters are cost-effective solutions for heating cylindrical surfaces, using mica sheets as insulation with embedded nickel-chrome resistance wires, encased in a stainless-steel sheath (typically SS 304). They operate at temperatures up to 900°F (482°C) and offer fast heat-up times with a maximum surface loading of 8 W/cm2. Energy-saving models include ceramic fiber-insulated jackets, reducing heat loss by approximately 20%. View Brochure

CERAMIC BEND HEATERS Ceramic band heaters are advanced heating elements designed for high-temperature and energy-efficient heating of cylindrical surfaces. Constructed with nickel-chrome resistance wires wound through interlocking ceramic tiles and insulated with high-temperature fiber, these heaters are encased in a durable metal sheath (usually stainless steel or aluminized steel). Their unique design allows for excellent heat retention and uniform heat distribution while reducing heat loss and power consumption—making them ideal for continuous and high-temperature industrial processes.
